Both the code-level finding and the spec's own declared reduction point the same direction, independently. Nothing in this brief proposes extending, amending, or working around either the fixture-satisfiability finding or the standing G1/G2 gates -- both remain exactly as frozen. What an agent session CAN productively do, at zero product-file cost, is: (1) reconfirm the existing hermetic composition-machinery tests are still green at today's exact-main tip (SLICE-1); (2) run the real controller invocation once, expecting and recording its fast-fail refusal on the unmet camp-01g/proof-02 predecessor chain, converting an inference into a live fact (SLICE-2); and (3) exercise the composition publisher itself against synthetic fixture inputs in scratch space (never touching tracked files) to live-confirm, rather than merely read, the static-gateReceiptId finding and the composer's hard-coded 'coverage-gap/minor' severity default -- a real, separate gap from fixture-satisfiability that this session found in the composer's own categorization logic (SLICE-3). Everything past that remains blocked on exactly the constraints the task charter names as owner-only (three genuine play sessions; a real second-collaborator APPROVED review, live-reverified this session via gh api: 1 collaborator, 0 required reviews on main) plus two structural gaps this brief additionally surfaces: R2.combat-browser, this node's second hard dependency, is entirely unscoped (zero taskKeys, no admission brief) and is itself blocked behind R2.combat's own open owner decision; and the composer's finding-severity categorization does not yet implement the delta spec's richer taxonomy, independent of any review-gate or witness-count concern.
